claims.text: The starting material is an initially single-phase, homogeneous high-entropy alloy without intermetallic precipitates or significant grain-boundary segregation.
Thermal aging can induce grain-boundary nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, and Mn in a high-entropy alloy.
Increasing aging temperature or duration will progressively increase grain-boundary nanoclustering.
Aging conditions can be selected that induce nanoclustering without causing precipitation, phase separation, or significant grain coarsening.
Grain-boundary nanoclustering reduces local grain-boundary cohesive strength.
Thermally activated atomic diffusion causes selected solutes to cluster at grain boundaries.
Nanoclustering weakens interatomic bonding at grain boundaries and lowers the energy required for intergranular decohesion.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion promotes a transition from ductile transgranular fracture to brittle intergranular cracking.
More prolonged or higher-temperature aging will reduce fracture toughness relative to freshly prepared specimens.
More prolonged or higher-temperature aging will increase the incidence of brittle intergranular cracking.
Freshly prepared baseline specimens exhibit high ductility and toughness.
Elevated-temperature loading can produce a hot-ductility drop and brittle intergranular fracture in a heat-treated alloy.
The proposed embrittlement is confined to service temperatures and stresses that permit nanoclustering while avoiding phase transformation, grain growth, and precipitation.
The proposed nanoclustering mechanism applies under both high- and low-temperature service loading regimes.
Impurity segregation and brittle grain-boundary second phases are established causes of grain-boundary weakening and crack initiation in conventional metals and alloys.
The quantitative relationship between nanoclustering and fracture-toughness loss is unknown and may be affected by trace impurities or grain-boundary morphology.
The hypothesis is falsified if specimens with increased measured nanoclustering do not show reduced fracture toughness or a shift toward brittle behavior.
